# Exact and approximate boundary first study

`first-observations.json` is a byte-for-byte copy of the frozen capture bundle:
145 original UTF-8 files, their paths, modes and SHA-256 identities, stored in
269,597 bytes. It retains six complete first projects, predictions, intended
commands, actual stdout/stderr and command records, all ten emitted artifacts,
the partial observation snapshot, the separate repair/counterexample and the
later host arithmetic script/result. No source or observation was overwritten.

This was an informed study with the Issues, adopted interpretations, Reference
and implementation available, using at most two physical quantum wires. The
fixed CLI/checker/source identities stayed unchanged during each observation.
Twenty-eight first calls and six follow-up calls produced 28 successes and
six refusals, with no timeout. Native process counts were not instrumented.
Successful proposal emission remains untrusted; selected hierarchy checks state
producer consistency, and ordinary validity is not an independent ideal request.

The original `tdg` program succeeds through ordinary project check/run/emission
but its selected hierarchy run/proposal emission refuses that primitive. The
separate `attempt-02` translates it to existing `phase[7,3]`: selected hierarchy
execution retains the negative imaginary amplitude, while ordinary finite
check/run refuses the static argument. Both outcomes remain first observations;
the repair does not expand phase syntax or reintroduce excluded #39/#63 work.

The six first sources distinguish T from identity, opposite phase signs,
coherently controlled scalar phase and complete observing behavior. Equal
measurement marginals do not establish equal residual/reference channels. The
later deliberate residual-Z `apply_contract` counterexample rejects through both
ordinary project and selected Raw checking. That is an existing exact-contract
refusal, not an approximation-certificate result or an all-reference proof from
the sampled distributions.

Seven later rational R8 host calculations retain nonzero, too-tight, phase,
zero, tensor and sequential-budget examples. They establish only their saved
host arithmetic results. A Frobenius witness needs a separate operator-norm
refinement; tensoring identity can inflate it, and composition needs checked
isometry premises. No native arithmetic-capacity/work proof is supplied.
Neither numerical agreement nor even a zero-labeled engineering bound grants
exact Meaning, capabilities, cleanup, constitutional PR or target-RS authority.
No approximation API or metric/bound certificate was exercised or implemented.

`scripts/test_exact_approx_baseline.py`, rooted by the ordinary Rust baseline
test, checks this history statically. It never executes a captured command or
Python script, extracts files, follows the recorded temporary paths, authenticates
binary provenance or proves source/runtime preservation. The remaining engineering
implementation and proof duties stay in Issues #31 and #163 under adopted #311.
